# Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

Kaplan et al. show that language model performance scales as a power law
with three quantities: model size, dataset size, and training compute.
The paper introduces the [[scaling-laws]] concept that has guided every
subsequent frontier model, including [[gpt-3]].

Key finding: bigger is reliably better, given enough data and compute.
The compute-optimal frontier was later refined by the Chinchilla paper,
which argued earlier models were undertrained.

Tags: scaling, training, compute.
